summary: Xi'an is well suited to heritage-led travel shaped by ancient capital atmosphere, city-wall space, Muslim Quarter energy, and strong historical identity.
transport_notes: Xi'an's core heritage zones are easiest to enjoy when grouped around the old city area.
Family and slower-paced plans should avoid stacking too many major historical stops in one day.
Evening food experiences work best when paired with old-city walking rather than distant site transfers.

budget_notes.low: Use the old city core, snack-heavy areas, and walkable landmark clustering to keep spending manageable.
budget_notes.medium: Combine one major heritage site, one old-city district, and one strong local food area each day.
budget_notes.high: Allow more breathing room between major heritage stops and include stronger dining moments.

trip_type_notes.student: Student plans in Xi'an should make history feel vivid, approachable, and well paired with affordable food.
trip_type_notes.solo: Solo plans should emphasize the city's historical depth and the meditative quality of old-city wandering.
trip_type_notes.couple: Couple plans should soften the history with evening walls, lantern light, and textured old-city atmosphere.
trip_type_notes.family: Family plans should keep movement simple, combine history with open space, and avoid museum fatigue.
